McLaren: McLaren has rolled out a fresh front wing and a reshaped engine cover, plus a small “halo winglet,” all aimed at smoothing the air over the car and giving extra grip in the high‑speed corners. They’ve also tweaked the rear‑wing endplates, rear‑suspension fairings and floor‑edge devices to tighten the rear aerodynamics, while new cooling‑louvre settings keep the power unit at its sweet spot on this hot circuit. In short, the package should make the car more stable through fast turns and keep the engine cooler, giving McLaren a better chance to fight at the front of the grid this weekend.
Mercedes F1 Team: The team has lowered the outer pieces of the front wing and blended them into the footplate, plus softened the front‑corner lip and opened up the cooling inlets, which gives cleaner air to the front of the car and keeps the power unit at optimal temperature. On the floor, the diffuser roof and several low‑downforce sections have been reshaped and new slots added, while the rear‑winglet has been reshuffled to fine‑tune rear grip. Together these tweaks should improve overall balance, give the drivers more consistent cornering and help them manage tyre wear throughout the weekend.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull has reshaped the front‑wing flaps to give the car a smoother, more predictable balance through the corners, while a new brake‑duct shape should keep the brakes cooler and more reliable over a full race distance. Small tweaks to the floor’s edge and forward sections add a little extra grip, helping the car stick to the track when the speed drops out of the corners. Finally, an optional cooling panel on the engine cover gives the team a safety valve against overheating, so they can push harder without worrying about reliability issues this weekend.
Scuderia Ferrari: Scuderia Ferrari did not submit any updates for this event.
Williams Racing: Williams has reshaped the front‑corner brake‑duct to channel air more efficiently, keeping the brakes cooler and giving the car a cleaner nose‑side airflow pack for the circuit’s demands. The front‑suspension fairings have been re‑profiled, smoothing the air that runs over the wheels to boost grip, while the exhaust tailpipe has been moved back a bit to tidy up the rear flow and add a touch of extra downforce. Together, these tweaks should translate into better tyre performance and a more stable rear end, helping the team extract every ounce of speed this weekend.
Racing Bulls / RB: Red Bull has reshaped the underside of the car with a fresh floor profile, giving the car a steadier “grip‑factory” feel in the corners. At the back, the rear‑corner vanes, the beam wing and even the exhaust‑tailpipe bracket have been re‑shaped to smooth the airflow and trim drag, meaning the RB will be more stable through fast turns and have a little extra bite on the straights this weekend. In short, the tweaks tighten up aero balance and should translate into better lap times on the track.
Aston Martin: Aston Martin did not submit any updates for this event.
Haas F1 Team: Haas has reshaped the side‑pod inlet, fine‑tuning the airflow that feeds the car’s aerodynamics and cooling. The tweak also nudges the floor, rear suspension and rear‑corner aero, giving the chassis a tighter, more predictable grip especially through the high‑speed corners. In short, the changes should make the car feel more stable and quicker over the whole weekend, giving the drivers a better chance to fight for points.
Audi F1 Team: Audi’s package this weekend is all about getting more grip and keeping the power unit happy. The team has reshaped the front and rear brake ducts and added fresh side‑pod louvers to improve cooling where the track demands it, while a tweaked diffuser winglet on the floor gives a little extra down‑force on the straights and corners. In short, the car should stay cooler and stick to the asphalt better, giving Audi a stronger launch and more consistent lap times.
Alpine F1 Team: Alpine rolled out a freshly reshaped floor and side‑pods, giving the car a cleaner airflow underneath that boosts overall down‑force without adding drag. They also tweaked the rear wing’s shape, tightening its grip on the back end for better stability through high‑speed corners. Together, the changes should make the car stick to the track more reliably this weekend, translating into quicker lap times and a stronger fight for points.
Cadillac: Cadillac has tweaked the front‑corner area, reshaping the leading‑edge lip and re‑routing the brake‑air flow for better cooling, and refined the diffuser’s lower winglet and its mounting to smooth out airflow under the car. The result is more stable brakes and a little extra down‑force where it counts, giving the team better grip and consistency over a race‑distance. In short, the car should stay cooler and stick to the track a bit tighter this weekend.
